## Simple SEIR -> POMP Skeleton

Deterministic models are possible to execute within POMP, but you need to use
what's known as a pomp skeleton



```{r libraries, echo=FALSE}
library(pomp)

# for the hypercube
library(lhs)

# for plotting
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)
library(grid)

# for posterior analysis
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(viridis)

# for parrallelization
library(parallel)
```

## Ghana Onset Data

We pull the date of onset from the Savannah, Ghana data to get the number of 
symptomatic cases, which we are using as a proxy for newly symptomatic YF cases

```{r ghana-parse-savannah-data, eval=TRUE}

# Country specific variables
country = "ghana"
region.pop = 653266
vacc_delay = 22
vacc_cov = 0.7

if (!exists("YF2021_2022_savannah")) {
  cat("Loading the Savannah case data\n")
  load("YF2021_2022_savannah_date.RData")
} else {
  cat("Case data already loaded\n")
}

column = "DateOfOnset"
# column = "DateSeenHealthFacility"

presenting_dates = YF2021_2022_savannah_date[[column]]

tab_all_dates <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(inherits(x, "Date"))
  
  # counts for dates that appear
  counts <- table(x)                 # names are "yyyy-mm-dd" as character
  counts <- as.integer(counts)
  names(counts) <- names(table(x))
  
  # full date range (includes dates not present)
  full <- seq(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), by = "day")
  out <- integer(length(full))
  names(out) <- as.character(full)
  
  # fill observed counts into the full vector
  out[names(counts)] <- counts
  
  out
}

d <- tab_all_dates(presenting_dates)

blank.count = 1

onset_data = c(rep(0, blank.count), d, rep(0, 365-length(d)-blank.count))

#Load TSI (temperature suitability index) components
load("savannah_TSI.RData")

# Data Manipulation
# 1. Convert the 'date' column to actual Date objects
# (Ensure the format matches your data, e.g., "%Y-%m-%d")
savannah_TSI$date <- as.Date(savannah_TSI$date)

# 2. Re-define the start date (now that the column is fixed)
start_date <- min(savannah_TSI$date)

# 3. NOW calculate the index
# This will now produce numbers (0, 31, 61...) instead of an error
savannah_TSI$time_idx <- as.numeric(savannah_TSI$date - start_date)

#Step function for temperature dependent parameters
# Ensure your data is sorted by date/time_idx
savannah_TSI <- savannah_TSI[order(savannah_TSI$time_idx), ]

# Create the step functions
# f = 0 means: "For any time t between 0 and 31, use the value at 0."
# rule = 2 means: "If t goes past the last date, just keep using the last value."

mu_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                         y = savannah_TSI$mu, 
                         method = "constant", 
                         f = 0, 
                         rule = 2)

a_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                        y = savannah_TSI$a, 
                        method = "constant", 
                        f = 0, 
                        rule = 2)

sigma_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                            y = savannah_TSI$sigma_v,
                            method = "constant", 
                            f = 0, 
                            rule = 2)
```

## South Sudan Onset Data

We pull the date of onset from the South Sudan data to get the number of symptomatic
cases, which we are using as a proxy for newly symptomatic YF cases

```{r parse-south-sudan-data, eval=FALSE}

# Country specific variables
country = "sudan"
region.pop = 663235
vacc_delay = 61
vacc_cov = 0.5

if (!exists("YF2023_sudan")) {
  cat("Loading the South Sudan case data\n")
  load("YF2023_sudan.RData")
} else {
  cat("Case data already loaded\n")
}

YF2023_sudan['combined'] = YF2023_sudan['cases_dead'] + YF2023_sudan['cases_alive']

column = "combined"

# The Savannah data is the date of presentation, while the South Sudan data is the count
# per day, in order.

blank.count = 1

raw_onset_data = unlist(YF2023_sudan[column])

onset_data = c(rep(0, blank.count), raw_onset_data, rep(0, 365-length(raw_onset_data)-blank.count))

#Load TSI (temperature suitability index) components
load("sudan_TSI.RData")

# 1. Convert the 'date' column to actual Date objects
# (Ensure the format matches your data, e.g., "%Y-%m-%d")
sudan_TSI$date <- as.Date(sudan_TSI$date)

# 2. Re-define the start date (now that the column is fixed)
start_date <- min(sudan_TSI$date)

# 3. NOW calculate the index
# This will now produce numbers (0, 31, 61...) instead of an error
sudan_TSI$time_idx <- as.numeric(sudan_TSI$date - start_date)

# Check the result
head(sudan_TSI$time_idx)

#Step function for temperature dependent parameters
# Ensure your data is sorted by date/time_idx
sudan_TSI <- sudan_TSI[order(sudan_TSI$time_idx), ]

# Create the step functions
# f = 0 means: "For any time t between 0 and 31, use the value at 0."
# rule = 2 means: "If t goes past the last date, just keep using the last value."

mu_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                         y = sudan_TSI$mu, 
                         method = "constant", 
                         f = 0, 
                         rule = 2)

a_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                        y = sudan_TSI$a, 
                        method = "constant", 
                        f = 0, 
                        rule = 2)

sigma_step_fun <- approxfun(x = sudan_TSI$time_idx, 
                            y = sudan_TSI$sigma_v,
                            method = "constant", 
                            f = 0, 
                            rule = 2)
```
## State definition

The skeleton model states.  We now add in an accumulator for new toxic cases
between observations

```{r state-definition}
## State names (match your model)
state_names <- c(
  "Sh","Eh","Ih","Ah","Th","Rh",
  "TotInf","TotDeath",
  "Sv","Ev","Iv",
  "Hsymp"
)
```

## Model Parameters

These are the pomp model parameters from Seth's SEIR model

```{r pomp-params}

model_pars <- list(
  Nh = region.pop, 
  
  # LHS PARAMETERS; not used in the parameters directly
  v_mult = NA_real_, # Multiplied by the human population to get the vector population
  Iv0 = NA_real_, # Initial number of infected mosquitoes
  # rho = 0.75,   # Case reporting probability
  rho = NA_real_,   # Case reporting probability
  
  # Varying as the grid before the LHS
  vacc_coverage = NA_real_, # What percentage of the population is previously covered
                       # by the vaccine.  In the SEIR: c(0.5, 0.6, 0.8)
  vacc_start_day = NA_real_,  # The day at which the vaccination campaign starts
                        # In the SEIR model, this varies: c(20, 60, 120)
  Ih0 = 1, # Initial number of infected humans
  
  # Model Fixed Parameters
  sigma_h=1/4,  # Human incubation rate (1/sigma_h = mean latent duration)
  gamma_h=1/4,  # Recovery rate from I and A
  eta=1/2,      # Progression rate from I -> T (Toxic)
  k=1/8,        # Toxic exit rate; how long do patients stay toxic? 1/8 =
                # mean toxic duration
  delta=0.12, #Ratio of symptomatic to asymptomatic individuals
  
  ########### THETA (Case fatality rate) ##############
  # General
  theta=0.095,  # Case fatality rate of those leaving T (Carlos)
  ##################### THETA #########################
  
  b=0.4,       # Probability that a bite from an infected mosquito infects
               # a human
  c=0.5,       # Probability that biting an infected human infects the mosquito
  xi=0.5,   # Relative infectiousness of asymptomatic vs symptomatic
  
  vacc_rate_per_person = 0.079 # Daily vaccination rate per person (Carlos)
)

```
## The deterministic skeleton

```{r skeleton-day-step}
yf_skeleton_C <- vectorfield(
  Csnippet("
    double Nh_current;
    double Nv_current;
    double lambda_h;
    double lambda_v;
    double current_vacc_flow;
    double new_infections;
    double new_deaths;
    double new_sympto;

    /* Current population totals */
    Nh_current = Sh + Eh + Ih + Ah + Th + Rh;
    Nv_current = Sv + Ev + Iv;

    /* Forces of infection */
    lambda_h = (a_t * b * Iv) / Nh_current;
    lambda_v = (a_t * c * (Ih + xi * Ah)) / Nh_current;

    /* Vaccination flow */
    if (t >= vacc_start_day + 10) {
      current_vacc_flow = vacc_rate_per_person * Sh;
    } else {
      current_vacc_flow = 0.0;
    }

    /* Incidence and death flows */
    new_infections = sigma_h * Eh;
    new_deaths     = theta * k * Th;
    new_sympto     = sigma_h * delta * Eh;

    /* Human derivatives */
    DSh = -lambda_h * Sh
          - current_vacc_flow;

    DEh = lambda_h * Sh
          - sigma_h * Eh;

    DIh = delta * sigma_h * Eh
          - eta * Ih;

    DAh = (1.0 - delta) * sigma_h * Eh
          - gamma_h * Ah;

    DTh = eta * Ih
          - k * Th;

    DRh = gamma_h * Ah
          + (1.0 - theta) * k * Th
          + current_vacc_flow;

    /* Mosquito derivatives */
    DSv = mu_v_t * Nv_current
          - lambda_v * Sv
          - mu_v_t * Sv;

    DEv = lambda_v * Sv
          - (sigma_v_t + mu_v_t) * Ev;

    DIv = sigma_v_t * Ev
          - mu_v_t * Iv;

    /* Cumulative-counter derivatives */
    DTotInf   = new_infections;
    DTotDeath = new_deaths;
    DHsymp    = new_sympto;
  ")
)
```

## The initial state of the skeleton

```{r pomp-init}

yf_rinit <- function(t0, ...) {
  p <- list(...)

  with(p, {
    Rh0 <- Nh * vacc_coverage
    Sh0 <- Nh - Rh0 - Ih0

    c(
      Sh = Sh0, Eh = 0, Ih = Ih0, Ah = 0, Th = 0, Rh = Rh0,
      TotInf = 0, TotDeath = 0,
      Sv = Nh * v_mult - Iv0, Ev = 0, Iv = Iv0, Hsymp = 0
    )
  })
}
```

## Pomp functions

Create the covariates here; mu, a and sigma, that depend on time

```{r pomp-stubs}

# Important here; both the ghana and the south sudan data have the same names
# and the same format; make sure we've properly selected the correct Data above
# before running

times <- 1:365

# Create the covariates
model_t0 <- 0

covariate_times <- seq(
  from = model_t0,
  to   = max(times) + 1,
  by   = 1
)

yf_covariates <- data.frame(
  time = covariate_times,

  mu_v_t = vapply(
    covariate_times,
    mu_step_fun,
    numeric(1)
  ),

  a_t = vapply(
    covariate_times,
    a_step_fun,
    numeric(1)
  ),

  sigma_v_t = vapply(
    covariate_times,
    sigma_step_fun,
    numeric(1)
  )
)

yf_covar_table <- covariate_table(
  yf_covariates,
  times = "time",
  order = "constant"
)

dat <- data.frame(time=times, onset=onset_data)
```

## Measurement Model

Now that we are introducing the case data, we need a measurement model
Previously I was clamping the value of mu, but this was causing nll problems
further down the line.

```{r measurement-model}
dmeasure <- function(onset, Hsymp, rho, ..., log) {
  if (is.na(onset)) return(if (log) 0 else 1)

  mu <- rho * Hsymp

  # exact handling when mu is 0 or negative (shouldn't be negative, but be safe)
  if (mu <= 0) {
    if (log) return(if (onset == 0) 0 else -Inf)
    else     return(if (onset == 0) 1 else 0)
  }

  dpois(onset, lambda = mu, log = log)
}

rmeasure <- function(Hsymp, rho, ...) {
  mu <- pmax(rho * Hsymp, 0)
  c(onset = rpois(1, lambda = mu))
}
```

## Define the pomp object

```{r pomp-object}
po <- pomp(
  data = dat,
  times = "time",
  t0 = model_t0,
  skeleton = yf_skeleton_C,
  rinit = yf_rinit,
  rmeasure = rmeasure,
  dmeasure = dmeasure,
  covar = yf_covar_table,
  statenames = state_names,
  paramnames = names(unlist(model_pars)),
  accumvars = "Hsymp",
  compile = TRUE
)
```

## LHS

We are looking to find sets of parameters that create outbreaks of YF that match
the epi curves of established outbreaks.  We will vary the parameters using
a latin hypercube sampling method.  Those variables we are looking at are defined
here

```{r lhs-params}

lhs.run.count <- 10000
random.seed <- 6232932 #abstract 10k seed

lhs.scenario.sample.count = 4400
lhs.scenario.sample.count.heatmap = 4400

lhs.spec <- list(
  rho     = list(type="unif", min=0.2,  max=1.0), #Reporting Rate
  Iv0     = list(type="int",  min=20,   max=500), #Initial Infected Vectors
  v_mult  = list(type="unif",  min=1,    max=8)   # Initial size of the vector population (times Human Pop)
)

```

## LHS Parameter generation

Now that we have identified all the parameters we would like to modify using 
the lhs, we have to create the new parameter sets

```{r lhs-parameter-generation}
lhs_sample <- function(n, spec, seed=1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  pnames <- names(spec)
  U <- randomLHS(n, length(pnames))
  colnames(U) <- pnames

  out <- as.data.frame(U)
  for (nm in pnames) {
    s <- spec[[nm]]
    u <- out[[nm]]
    if (s$type == "unif") {
      out[[nm]] <- s$min + u*(s$max - s$min)
    } else if (s$type == "log") {
      out[[nm]] <- exp(log(s$min) + u*(log(s$max) - log(s$min)))
    } else if (s$type == "int") {
      out[[nm]] <- as.integer(round(s$min + u*(s$max - s$min)))
    } else {
      stop("Unknown type: ", s$type)
    }
  }
  out
}

```
## This will run one instance of the skeleton

```{r lhs-run-single}
# Now we create a function that runs the model once:
# For the first stage LHS
run.single <- function(base_params, varied_row) {
  params <- base_params
  params[names(varied_row)] <- as.list(varied_row)

  tr <- trajectory(po, params=params, format="data.frame")

  total <- sum(tr$Hsymp, na.rm=TRUE)
  peak  <- max(tr$Hsymp, na.rm=TRUE)
  tpeak <- tr$time[which.max(tr$Hsymp)]

  c(total_Hsymp=total, peak_Hsymp=peak, t_peak=tpeak)
}

# This is the second stage scenario runner
run.single.params <- function(base_params, varied_row) {
  params <- base_params
  params[names(varied_row)] <- as.list(varied_row)

  tr <- trajectory(po, params=params, format="data.frame")

  total <- sum(tr$Hsymp, na.rm=TRUE)
  peak  <- max(tr$Hsymp, na.rm=TRUE)
  tpeak <- tr$time[which.max(tr$Hsymp)]
  total_death <- sum(tr$TotDeath, na.rm=TRUE)

  list("results" = c(total_Hsymp=total, peak_Hsymp=peak, t_peak=tpeak, total_death=total_death, rho=params$rho), "tr"=tr)
}

```

# Running the LHS model parameter exploration

Using r parallel for parallelization

```{r run-lhs}
# Now, we have the ability to generate parameters and run one simulation, put
# them together and run multiple simulations

# how many cores do we went to use?
ncores <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)

# This is run stage two LHS
run.parallel.params <- function(run_params, lhs_params, core.count) {
  stopifnot(is.data.frame(lhs_params) || is.matrix(lhs_params))
  idx <- seq_len(nrow(lhs_params))

  res_list <- parallel::mclapply(
    idx,
    function(i) run.single.params(run_params, lhs_params[i, ]),
    mc.cores = core.count
  )

  # Extract the per-run named vectors
  results_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(res_list, `[[`, "results"))
  res <- as.data.frame(results_mat, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # Keep LHS parameters alongside results (assumes lhs_params is data.frame-like)

  # Extract trajectories (list of data.frames), preserving order
  traj_list <- lapply(res_list, `[[`, "tr")

  list(res = res, traj = traj_list)
}


# This is the stage 1 lhs models executor
run.lhs.parallel <- function(run_params, lhs_params, core.count) {

  # create the sequential index for the loop
  idx <- seq_len(nrow(lhs_params))
  
  res_list <- mclapply(
    idx,
    function(i) {
      run.single(run_params, lhs_params[i, ])
    },
    mc.cores = core.count
  )
  
  res <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, res_list))
  res <- cbind(res, lhs_params)
  
  res
}

```
# Similarity to baseline

```{r likelihood}

# Now, we are looking for results within a certain threshold. Use the NLL 
# (negative log likelihood) function as a vehicle to rank the results

calc.nll.parallel <- function(run_params, lhs_params, core.count) {

  est <- colnames(lhs_params)

  # Complete parameter vector needed to construct traj_objfun
  init_params <- unlist(run_params)

  # Supply valid initial values for all LHS-estimated parameters.
  # These are subsequently replaced on every call to ofun().
  init_params[est] <- as.numeric(lhs_params[1, est])

  ofun <- traj_objfun(
    po,
    est = est,
    params = init_params
  )

  idx <- seq_len(nrow(lhs_params))

  nll <- unlist(mclapply(
    idx,
    function(i) {

      par_i <- setNames(
        as.numeric(lhs_params[i, est]),
        est
      )

      ofun(par = par_i)
    },
    mc.cores = core.count
  ))

  nll

}

low.runs.parallel <- function(results, run_params, lhs_params, core.count, nll.prox = 10) {
  est <- colnames(lhs_params)
  # Keep those within nll.prox NLL units of best
  keep <- results$nll <= (min(results$nll, na.rm=TRUE) + nll.prox)
  res_kept <- results[keep, ]
  table(keep)
  
  idx_kept <- which(keep)   # or keep, depending what you’re saving
  
  # Re-calculate the trajectory of the runs that were successful
  traj_kept <- mclapply(
    idx_kept,
    function(i) {
      params <- unlist(run_params)
      params[est] <- as.numeric(lhs_params[i, est])
  
      tr <- trajectory(po, params = params, format = "data.frame")
      tr$run_id <- i
      tr$nll    <- results$nll[i]
      tr
    },
    mc.cores = ncores
  )
  
  list(idx_kept = idx_kept, traj_kept = traj_kept, res_kept = res_kept)
}

```

# Posterior examiniation

We look at res_kept for the best runs, and examine their parameter values
to check whether we can narrow our hypercube parameter ranges

```{r lhs-posteriors}

# Calculate bins for each parameter
bin_one_param <- function(df, bins) {
  v <- df$value
  v_max <- max(v)
  v_min <- 0

  brks <- seq(v_min, v_max, length.out = bins + 1)
  if (v_max == 0) brks <- seq(0, 1, length.out = bins + 1)  # degenerate guard

  b <- findInterval(v, brks, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
  b <- pmin(pmax(b, 1), length(brks) - 1)

  df %>%
    mutate(bin = b) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(
      xmin = brks[first(bin)],
      xmax = brks[first(bin) + 1],
      count = n(),
      nll_med = median(nll, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

plot.posteriors <- function(results, params, bin.count = 50, title.text) {

  # Clean up and pivot the data
  plot_df <- results %>%
    select(any_of(c(params, "nll"))) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = any_of(params), names_to = "param", values_to = "value") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(nll))
  
  # Apply the bin calculating function above to each parameter
  binned <- plot_df %>%
    group_by(param) %>%
    group_modify(~ bin_one_param(.x, bins = bin.count)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Plot the histograms
  plot <- ggplot(binned) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = count, fill = nll_med)) +
    facet_wrap(~ param, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
    # Start at zero
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA)) +
    # Legend
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey10", high = "grey90", name = "median NLL") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "count", title = title.text)
  # print(plot)
  invisible(plot)
}

```

# Baseline-LHS

We now want to produce a single, large LHS for the scenario we are mapping

```{r single-baseline-lhs}

# Single version params
vacc_delay_scenario <- vacc_delay
vacc_coverage_scenario <- vacc_cov

 #Create a grid of all combinations
scenario_grid <- expand.grid(#rr = relative_infectivity,
                             delay = vacc_delay_scenario,
                             coverage = vacc_coverage_scenario)

# scenario.count = nrow(scenario_grid)
# LHS to examine during posterior analysis
posterior.params <- c("rho", "Iv0", "v_mult")

# For the cumulative plots, create a cumulative data set

dat_cum <- dat %>%
  arrange(time) %>%
  mutate(Cobs = cumsum(onset)) 

iter.str = sprintf("%s Baseline LHS, Size %g", tools::toTitleCase(country), lhs.run.count)
 
cat(iter.str)
  
vals <- list(delay=vacc_delay_scenario, coverage=vacc_coverage_scenario)
params_copy <- model_pars
  
# Grid params
params_copy$vacc_start_day <- vals$delay
params_copy$vacc_coverage <- vals$coverage
  
# Sample the LHS
lhs_params <- lhs_sample(n=lhs.run.count, spec=lhs.spec, seed=random.seed)
  
# Scenario updated, run model:
res <- run.lhs.parallel(params_copy, lhs_params, ncores)
res$nll <- calc.nll.parallel(params_copy, lhs_params, ncores)
  
# Calculate within nll.prox points, and retrieve those trajectories
traj_results = low.runs.parallel(res, params_copy, lhs_params, ncores, nll.prox = 10)

traj_kept <- traj_results$traj_kept
idx_kept <- traj_results$idx_kept
res_kept <- traj_results$res_kept

names(traj_kept) <- paste0("lhs_", idx_kept)

title = sprintf("Delay %g, Coverage %.0f%%",
                vacc_delay, vacc_cov * 100)
  
```



```{r baseline-plots}

## build a long data.frame of trajectories
traj_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(traj_kept), function(i) {
  tr <- traj_kept[[i]]
  data.frame(
    traj_id  = i,
    time     = tr$time,
    Hsymp    = tr$Hsymp,
    obs_onset = tr$Hsymp * res_kept$rho[i],
    TotDeath = tr$TotDeath,
    nll      = tr$nll[1],   # assumes nll is per-trajectory
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

band <- traj_df %>%
  group_by(time) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(obs_onset, na.rm = TRUE),
    lo   = quantile(obs_onset, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    hi   = quantile(obs_onset, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

display.prefix = if (country == "sudan") { "South " } else { "" }

baseline.traj.plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = dat, aes(x = time, y = onset), shape = 16) +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(x = time, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = band, aes(x = time, y = mean), linewidth = 0.8) +
```

# Weighted Resample
After the baseline run, we want to do a weighted resample, so do that here
```{r weighted-resample}
df_kept <- as.data.frame(res_kept, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# How many results to keep?
n <- lhs.scenario.sample.count

# Distribute the weights
w <- 1 / exp(df_kept$nll)
w <- w / sum(w)

# Do the sampling
sampled_idx <- sample.int(nrow(df_kept), size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = w)

# Parse out the results
sampled_kept <- df_kept[sampled_idx,]
params_10k <- sampled_kept[, c("rho", "Iv0", "v_mult")]
```

# Heatmap Only

  We want the heatmaps to have the same results as the data tables, but that will
  only happen if we have the same number of iterations; making the heatmap with all
  the extraneous data is taxing for RAM, write a secondary scenario executor that
  runs the heatmap code.  Bypasses 'run_results' and goes right to 'out'
  
```{r run-heatmap-scenarios, eval=FALSE}

vacc_delay_scenarios <- c(20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120)
vacc_coverage_scenarios <- c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9)

 #Create a grid of all combinations
scenario_grid <- expand.grid(delay = vacc_delay_scenarios, 
                             coverage = vacc_coverage_scenarios)

scenario.count = nrow(scenario_grid)
# LHS to examine during posterior analysis
posterior.params <- c("rho", "Iv0", "v_mult")


# We want to pull from the sampled weights, rather than all the returned values.
param.values <- params_10k
# param.values <- baseline.out$res_kept[,c("rho","Iv0","v_mult")]

good.param.count <- nrow(param.values)

# For the cumulative plots, create a cumulative data set

dat_cum <- dat %>%
  arrange(time) %>%
  mutate(Cobs = cumsum(onset)) 


out <- vector("list", scenario.count)

for (idx in seq_len(scenario.count)) {

  cat(sprintf(
    "Running scenario %g/%g (%g runs)\n",
    idx,
    scenario.count,
    good.param.count
  ))

  vals <- scenario_grid[idx, ]
  params_copy <- model_pars

  params_copy$vacc_start_day <- vals$delay
  params_copy$vacc_coverage  <- vals$coverage

  res_list <- run.parallel.params(
    params_copy,
    param.values,
    ncores
  )

  out[[idx]] <- list(
    res_kept = res_list$res[, c(
      "rho",
      "total_Hsymp"
    ), drop = FALSE]
  )

  rm(res_list)
  gc(FALSE)
}
```

#Heatmap

We want to produce a single figure that can represent multiple data points across the simulations.

```{r heatmap}

scenario_grid$cluster_id <- seq_len(nrow(scenario_grid))

# How do we interpret the values from the runs? Accept the values, the nll values
# and the method: 
#    'mean' - mean of all the values
reduce_vals <- function(vals) {
  # Match.arg will return the user specified value or the first value in the method vector above
  # This would be the "best" value, ie the one with the lowest nll
  mean(vals)
}


# Extract a numeric vector from res_kept column (one value per accepted run)
extract_from_rescol <- function(res_col) {
  force(res_col)

  function(cluster) {
    rk <- cluster$res_kept

    list(
      vals = as.numeric(rk[[res_col]] * rk$rho)
    )
  }
}

# Extract a numeric vector from each trajectory (one value per accepted run)
extract_from_traj <- function(traj_fun) {
  # traj_fun is a function that operates over the entire column, reducing it to one value.
  # So "sum", "max", "min", etc.
  force(traj_fun)
  function(cluster) {
    rk <- cluster$res_kept
    tk <- cluster$traj_kept
    
    vals <- vapply(tk, function(tr) as.numeric(traj_fun(tr)), numeric(1))
    list(vals = vals)
  }
}

make_heatmap <- function(out,
                         # value.clamp = 1300,
                         extractor,
                         delays = vacc_delay_scenarios,
                         coverages = vacc_coverage_scenarios,
                         fill_label = "value",
                         title = NULL,
                         subtitle = NULL,
                         na_fill = "grey90") {

  grid <- scenario_grid

  # Use the extractor and the reducer to compute one scalar per cluster
  grid$value <- vapply(out, function(cluster) {
    ex <- extractor(cluster)         
    reduce_vals(ex$vals)
    # min (reduce_vals(ex$vals), value.clamp)
  }, numeric(1))
  
  ok <- is.finite(grid$value) & grid$value > 0
  
  grid$text_col <- "#111111"
  
  scaled_value <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(grid))
  
  scaled_value[ok] <- scales::rescale(
    log10(grid$value[ok]),
    to = c(0, 1)
  )

  grid$text_col[ok & scaled_value < 0.55] <- "#F2F2F2"
  
  # We also want to display the actual value in the cell, not the clamped value
  grid$orig <- vapply(out, function(cluster) {
    ex <- extractor(cluster)
    floor(reduce_vals(ex$vals))
  }, numeric(1))
  
  tile_width  <- min(diff(sort(unique(grid$delay))))
  tile_height <- min(diff(sort(unique(grid$coverage))))
  
  highlight_cell <- grid %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      delay == if (country == "ghana") { 20 } else { 60 },
      coverage == if (country == "ghana") { 0.70 } else { 0.50 }
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = delay, y = coverage, fill = value)) +
    geom_tile(color = NA) +
    
    geom_tile(
      data = highlight_cell,
      aes(x = delay, y = coverage),
      width = tile_width,
      height = tile_height,
      fill = NA,
      color = "#E6E6E6",
      linewidth = 0.8,
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    
    geom_text(
      aes(label = round(orig, 1), color=text_col),
      # color = "black",
      # color = text_col,
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 2
    ) + scale_color_identity() +
    viridis::scale_fill_viridis(
      option = "C",
      na.value = na_fill,
      trans="log10",
      labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = delays) +
    scale_y_reverse(breaks = coverages) + 
    labs(x = "Vaccination start delay (days)",
         y = "Vaccination coverage",
         fill = fill_label,
         title = title,
         subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_minimal()

  list(grid = grid, plot = p)
}
```

```{r figures}
# Weighted Mean of rho values from the kept list from
# the initial LHS

weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w >= 0
  x <- x[ok]
  w <- w[ok]

  ord <- order(x)
  x <- x[ord]
  w <- w[ord]

  w <- w / sum(w)
  cw <- cumsum(w)

  sapply(probs, function(p) {
    x[which(cw >= p)[1]]
  })
}

posterior_summary <- function(x, w) {
  qs <- weighted_quantile(x, w)

  c(
    mean = weighted.mean(x, w, na.rm = TRUE),
    lo95 = qs[1],
    hi95 = qs[2]
  )
}

nll <- res_kept$nll

w <- exp(-(nll - min(nll, na.rm = TRUE)))

rho_summary <- posterior_summary(res_kept$rho, w)
v_mult_summary <- posterior_summary(res_kept$v_mult, w)
Iv0_summary <- posterior_summary(res_kept$Iv0, w)

rho_summary
v_mult_summary
Iv0_summary
```
